name: Columbia Heights Rezoning

status.headline: The formal ULURP clock has not started
paragraphs: The application is filed with City Planning [[zap]]. The environmental review is underway, and the public scoping meeting took place on March 12, 2026 [[scopenotice]]. The next step is DCP issuing the Final Scope of Work, which its system targets for Nov 16–26, 2026 [[zap]]. After that, the applicant prepares the Draft EIS. Once City Planning certifies the application as complete, the 7-month ULURP clock starts with Community Board 2 [[ulurp]].

No ULURP hearing or vote has been scheduled. Community Board 2, the Borough President, the City Planning Commission and the City Council have all recorded nothing yet [[zap]]. The only CPC date in DCP's system is a review session listed for May 17, 2027 [[zap]]. That's probably the pre-certification review, which would put certification in late spring 2027.

Scoping comments aren't public yet. DCP publishes them, with its responses, in the Final Scope [[ds]]. Press coverage in March found residents supportive of housing but worried about the added height. Council Member Restler said he expects "a good solution" and stressed protecting Brooklyn Bridge views from the Promenade [[ny1]].

name: One Montague Place (205 & 181 Montague)
address: 205 Montague St at Cadman Plaza West, with air rights from 181 Montague St

status.headline: Built as of right, so there's no public review to track
paragraphs: Construction started in July 2026 after demolition of the office building finished in June [[sixsqft,holt]]. Completion is targeted for 2029, and condo sales are expected to launch in 2027 [[sixsqft]]. The condo offering plan was submitted to the State Attorney General on Feb 2, 2026 and is awaiting acceptance [[cityrealty]].

The tower needed no rezoning: City Planning has no application for either lot, so there is no ULURP, Community Board vote or Council vote. Its extra height comes from a zoning lot merger: in May 2026 the developer bought 181 Montague's unused development rights for $4,182,000 [[acrisair]] and recorded a zoning lot declaration covering 205 and 181 Montague, the 195 Montague condos and 142–146 Pierrepont [[acriszone]]. Saint Ann's School is a party to one of the agreements [[acrissage]]. An "air rights subdivision" for 181 Montague followed at the Buildings Department on Oct 29, 2026 [[dobair]].

The landmark bank building at 181 Montague stays. Any change to its exterior would need a public Landmarks hearing [[lpc]]. What's left to watch is construction permits and complaints, the offering plan's acceptance and sales, and anything filed for 181 itself.

It's being built on a zoning lot merged with its neighbors [[acriszone]], including the landmark People's Trust Company Building at 181 Montague, whose unused air rights were bought for the tower [[acrisair]].

name: Ritz-Carlton Residences (Hotel Bossert)

status.headline: Landmarks signed off; building permits are next
paragraphs: The Landmarks Preservation Commission approved the revised plan 9–0 on Sept 1, 2026, after hearing the first version on June 23 and sending it back [[pineapple]]. The approval covers a 15th-floor rooftop addition set back from the street, changes to the 13th-floor cornice, and mechanical equipment moved down to the 12th-floor roof [[pineapple,sixsqft]].

The developer filed the conversion with the Buildings Department on Oct 22, 2026 (job B01443511: "convert existing 14-story hotel to residences and add a 1-story addition", with an amended certificate of occupancy) [[dobconv]]. It's in plan review [[dobconv]]. Scaffolding, a sidewalk shed and facade restoration permits are already issued [[dobscaf,dobshed]].

The condo offering plan was submitted to the Attorney General on July 30, 2026 and is awaiting acceptance [[pineapple]]. No City Planning approval is needed: residential use is allowed under the R6 zoning [[pluto]].

name: 120 Court Street

status.headline: Demolition underway; the new building's plans are still in review
paragraphs: Rogers Equities bought the site from the Sorkin family for $30 million [[co]] (deed recorded Apr 30, 2026, to Atlantic Court NY LLC [[deed]], with about $35M in acquisition financing [[loan1,loan2]]). Walgreens closed in June 2026 [[co]] and demolition followed [[yimby]].

The new building application (DOB job B01379434, filed March 30, 2026 [[bldup]]) is still working through plan review: several of its work types have objections from DOB examiners, and the newest support-of-excavation filing (Nov 12) is waiting for an examiner [[dobnb]]. The zoning allows the building as of right, so there's no public review.

Plans call for 75 rental units over ground-floor retail [[co,bldup]], built under the state's 485-x tax incentive [[co]], which comes with affordability requirements [[hpd485x]]. Completion is posted for fall 2027 [[gensa]] (one listing says early 2028 [[cityrealty]]).

name: BQE Central (the triple cantilever)
address: I-278 from Atlantic Ave to Sands St, under the Promenade

status.headline: Scoping is underway; written comments are still open
paragraphs: Mayor Mamdani announced the plan on Aug 24, 2026: a full rehabilitation of the existing structure, said to extend its life about 40 years, to around 2080 [[mayor26]]. NYC DOT issued the Draft Scope of Work for the environmental impact statement on Oct 2, 2026 [[scope]] and held public scoping meetings on Nov 10 (in person, City Tech) and Nov 12 (Zoom) [[enb1007,dotpage]].

The written comment deadline was Nov 23, 2026 in the official notice [[enb1007]]; press reports it was extended to Jan 11, 2027 [[sb1116]]. DOT's page hadn't been updated when last checked, so confirm with DOT before relying on the later date. Comments go to BQECentral@dot.nyc.gov [[dotpage]].

Next: a Final Scope in early 2027, the Draft EIS with a public hearing in late 2027, and the Final EIS in 2028 [[dotpage]]. The sources disagree on when construction starts: 2029 in the Draft Scope [[scope]], 2030 in the Mayor's announcement [[mayor26]]. Work would finish before 2040 [[scope]]. Some parkland changes would need a ULURP starting around 2028 [[sb1116,faq]].

intro: The city-owned 1.5-mile stretch of the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway from Atlantic Avenue to Sands Street, with 21 bridges and structures, including the 0.4-mile triple cantilever built in 1954 that carries the Brooklyn Heights Promenade [[scope]]. The city plans to rehabilitate it, not replace it, using temporary bypass highways while the cantilever is repaired [[mayor26,scope]].
facts: Rehabilitate all 21 structures; replace the Columbia Heights overpass superstructure; new drainage and railings [[scope]]
Two each way, as today; no new capacity or interchange changes [[scope]]
A temporary two-level highway over Furman St, Atlantic Ave to Columbia Heights, below the Promenade [[scope]]
From Columbia Heights, possibly above the Brooklyn Bridge approach, through Dumbo to west of the Manhattan Bridge [[scope,sb1001]]
More than 130,000 vehicles a day, about 13,000 of them trucks [[scope]]
No federal grants; ~$800M in applications were rejected in 2024 [[politicsny]]
